title: What is Data Science?
q: Which of these is the best one-sentence definition of data science?
options: Turning data into decisions you can defend, using statistics, computation and domain knowledge
Building dashboards that show company KPIs
Training deep neural networks on large datasets
Writing SQL queries to extract reports
explain: Dashboards (BI), networks (ML engineering) and SQL are parts of the toolkit; the discipline itself is decision support with evidence.

title: What is Data Science?
q: A dataset of salaries has one entry of 9,000,000 while the rest are around 45,000. Which summary best describes a typical salary?
options: Median, because it is robust to the extreme value
Mean, because it uses all the data
Maximum, because it is the true top earner
Standard deviation, because it measures spread
explain: One extreme value drags the mean far above the typical value; the median stays stable.

title: What is Data Science?
q: What is the FIRST step of a data science project?
options: Frame the decision the work should support
explain: Every later choice (metric, validation, deliverable) follows from the framing step.

title: What is Data Science?
q: Which statement about the workflow is TRUE?
options: Cleaning and validation usually dominate total project time
Modelling usually dominates total project time
Exploration is unnecessary if you already have a hypothesis
Monitoring ends when the model is deployed
explain: In practice 60-80% of effort goes to acquiring, cleaning and validating data.

title: What is Data Science?
q: A stakeholder says 'just make the model accurate'. What is the professional response?
options: Ask which decision the prediction informs and what a false positive costs
Use deep learning because it is most accurate
explain: Accuracy is only meaningful against a decision cost. Phase 10 turns this into metric selection.

title: Data Analyst vs Data Scientist vs ML Engineer vs AI Engineer
q: Which artefact best distinguishes a data analyst from a data scientist?
options: Analyst owns reports and experiments; scientist owns questions and models
Analyst uses Excel; scientist uses Python
Analyst works in marketing; scientist works in product
Analyst is junior; scientist is senior
explain: The distinguishing factor is the owned artefact, not the tool or seniority.

title: Data Analyst vs Data Scientist vs ML Engineer vs AI Engineer
q: Who is typically on call when a model service degrades at 2 a.m.?
explain: Production service ownership defines the ML engineer role; this also explains the software engineering emphasis in that job family.

title: Data Analyst vs Data Scientist vs ML Engineer vs AI Engineer
q: Which skill is shared by ALL four roles and most often under-weighted by beginners?
explain: Every role must explain results to someone; that is why Day 79 and Phases 16 emphasise storytelling.

title: Data Analyst vs Data Scientist vs ML Engineer vs AI Engineer
q: An analyst job description lists experimentation. What is being tested?
options: Whether an intervention caused a change (A/B testing)
explain: Experimentation is causal testing, covered in depth on Day 133.

title: The Data Science Workflow
q: Which element makes a problem statement testable?
options: A named baseline and a numeric target with a horizon
explain: Without a baseline and target you cannot tell afterwards whether you succeeded.

title: The Data Science Workflow
q: Where do most data science projects fail?
explain: Technical failure is recoverable; wrong-question failure is not.

title: The Data Science Workflow
q: What belongs in data/raw?
options: Immutable copies of source data, never edited by hand
explain: Raw must stay pristine so any cleaning step can be re-derived and audited.

title: The Data Science Workflow
q: A stakeholder wants 'the most accurate model'. Which question best redirects them?
options: Which decision does a prediction inform, and what does each error type cost?
How much data do we have?
explain: Error costs determine the metric, and the metric determines the model choice.

title: The Data Science Workflow
q: Why fix a random seed and an as-of date in config?
options: So results are reproducible and comparable across reruns
explain: Reproducibility is a precondition for comparison, debugging and trust.

title: Setting Up Your Python Environment
q: You installed pandas but the notebook says ModuleNotFoundError. Most likely cause?
options: The notebook is using a different interpreter
You need to restart your computer
explain: Print sys.executable and compare with the interpreter where you installed pandas.

title: Setting Up Your Python Environment
q: Which file should be committed for reproducibility?
explain: Pin lists are small, portable and rebuildable; environment folders are not.

title: Setting Up Your Python Environment
q: Why is `python -m pip install X` preferred to bare `pip install X`?
options: It guarantees the pip belonging to the active interpreter is used
explain: Bare pip can resolve to another interpreter's pip on PATH - a classic silent failure.

title: Setting Up Your Python Environment
q: What is the main advantage of one environment per project?
options: Upgrading one project cannot break another
It removes the need for tests
explain: Isolation prevents dependency conflicts across projects.

title: Setting Up Your Python Environment
q: Where should data paths be relative to?
options: The project root, kept stable for notebooks and scripts
explain: Stable roots keep relative paths working when the project moves or runs in CI.

title: Jupyter, Colab, Packages and Reproducibility
q: Why can a notebook show results that its saved code cannot reproduce?
options: Outputs are stored in the file while variables live in the kernel, so cell order matters
explain: Restart & Run All is the test that the file alone is sufficient.

title: Jupyter, Colab, Packages and Reproducibility
q: Which magic measures the runtime of a single heavy cell?
explain: %%time is a cell magic for one run; %timeit repeats a line many times for statistics.

title: Jupyter, Colab, Packages and Reproducibility
q: What is the best home for logic you will reuse in three notebooks?
options: A module in src/ imported by each notebook
explain: Importable code can be tested, versioned and reused without drift.

title: Jupyter, Colab, Packages and Reproducibility
q: Before committing a notebook that calls an external API, you should:
options: Remove outputs containing keys and load secrets from environment variables
explain: Output cells frequently leak tokens; prevention is cheaper than rotating keys.

title: Jupyter, Colab, Packages and Reproducibility
q: What does %whos show?
options: Variables currently alive in the kernel
explain: A quick memory/state inspector, useful before and after restarts.

title: Variables, Data Types and Operators
q: After `a = [1,2]; b = a; b.append(3)`, what is `len(a)`?
options: 3 - both names reference the same list
explain: Assignment binds names to the same object.

title: Variables, Data Types and Operators
q: What does `matrix.copy()` do for a nested list?
options: Copies the outer list only; inner lists remain shared
explain: It is a shallow copy - the exact source of 'my original changed' bugs.

title: Variables, Data Types and Operators
q: Which comparison is correct for two computed floats?
explain: Binary floating point representation error makes exact equality unreliable.

title: Variables, Data Types and Operators
q: What does `-7 % 2` evaluate to in Python?
explain: The result takes the sign of the divisor, unlike C-style implementations.

title: Variables, Data Types and Operators
q: Why is `isinstance(True, int)` True?
options: bool is a subclass of int
explain: A real gotcha when validating numeric inputs - check bool explicitly if it matters.

title: Strings in Depth
q: What does 'Data Science'[5:12] return?
explain: Index 5 is 'S'; the stop index 12 is exclusive, so 'Science'.

title: Strings in Depth
q: Which is the efficient way to build a large string from many parts?
options: Collect parts in a list and use ''.join(parts)
Use f-strings in a loop with +
explain: join allocates once; += in a loop is O(n^2) because strings are immutable.

title: Strings in Depth
q: What is wrong with float('AED 1,299.00')?
options: Raises ValueError - clean the text first
explain: Currency symbols and separators must be removed before casting.

title: Strings in Depth
q: Which formatting shows 0.8734 as '87.3%'?
explain: The % spec multiplies by 100 and appends the sign; .1 controls decimals.

title: Strings in Depth
q: Two visually identical strings compare unequal. The best first diagnostic is:
explain: repr exposes invisible characters like non-breaking space or zero-width space.

title: Lists and Tuples
q: What does `lst = [3,1,2]; print(lst.sort())` output?
explain: sort() mutates in place and returns None.

title: Lists and Tuples
q: Which structure gives O(1) average membership testing?
explain: Sets (and dict keys) are hash-based; lists and tuples require linear scans.

title: Lists and Tuples
q: What is the result of `matrix = [[1,2],[3,4]]; r = matrix[0]; r.append(5)`?
explain: matrix[0] returns a reference to the inner list, so appending through r is visible in matrix.

title: Lists and Tuples
q: Why can a tuple be a dictionary key but a list cannot?
options: Tuples are hashable because they are immutable
explain: Hashability requires immutability so the key's hash cannot change while it is in the dict.

title: Lists and Tuples
q: Best way to return two values from a function?
options: return a, b and unpack at the call site
explain: Returning a tuple is idiomatic, type-safe and does not abuse globals or strings.

title: Sets and Dictionaries
q: Which answers 'customers present in both datasets'?
explain: & is intersection: members present in both.

title: Sets and Dictionaries
q: Why does `{[1,2]: 'x'}` raise TypeError?
options: Lists are unhashable, so they cannot be dict keys
Dicts can only have string keys
explain: Mutability means the hash could change, breaking the hash table. Use a tuple instead.

title: Sets and Dictionaries
q: `d.get('k')` versus `d['k']` when 'k' is missing:
explain: Choose based on whether absence is normal (get) or a bug (direct indexing).

title: Sets and Dictionaries
q: Which preserves insertion order while removing duplicates from a list?
explain: A dict preserves insertion order; converting back to a list gives ordered dedup. Sets are unordered.

title: Sets and Dictionaries
q: A pipeline reports 1000 rows and 950 unique user ids. Which statement is safe?
options: Some users generated multiple events in this window
The id column is a float
explain: Duplicates are expected in event logs; the question is whether they should be deduplicated for your metric.

title: Indexing and Slicing Mastery
q: What is the length of `[1,2,3,4,5][1:4]`?
explain: stop - start = 4 - 1 = 3 elements: 2, 3, 4.

title: Indexing and Slicing Mastery
q: What does `'abcdef'[::-1]` return?
explain: A negative step reverses the sequence.

title: Indexing and Slicing Mastery
explain: Positive step with start > stop returns empty; you need [3:1:-1] to go backwards.

title: Indexing and Slicing Mastery
q: For a NumPy array, `arr[1:3][0] = 99` will:
options: Modify arr, because basic slicing returns a view
explain: NumPy slices are views; use .copy() if you need an independent array.

title: Indexing and Slicing Mastery
q: Which slice takes the last 5 elements?
explain: Negative start counts from the end and an omitted stop runs to the end.

title: Conditions and Branching Logic
q: With `if spend >= 2000: 'Silver' elif spend >= 5000: 'Gold'`, what does spend=6000 return?
options: Silver - the first matching branch wins
explain: Classic ordering bug: the broader condition must come later.

title: Conditions and Branching Logic
q: Which expression is correct for checking a possibly-None value in numpy/pandas code?
options: if value is not None and value > 5
if not value == None and value > 5
if value is None or value > 5
explain: Identity check for None plus short-circuit protects the comparison.

title: Conditions and Branching Logic
q: Why does `(arr > 2) & (arr < 5)` need parentheses?
options: Bitwise operators bind tighter than comparisons
explain: Without parentheses Python evaluates arr > (2 & arr) etc., producing wrong or erroring code.

title: Conditions and Branching Logic
q: An empty list in a condition evaluates as:
explain: Empty containers are falsy - the basis of `if not rows`.

title: Conditions and Branching Logic
q: Best refactor for a 5-level nested if in a cleaning function?
options: Guard clauses with early returns or small named functions
explain: Flat code with named rules is testable and reviewable.

title: Loops and Iteration Tools
q: Which loop form gives both index and value?
explain: enumerate yields (index, value) pairs; you can set start=1 for human numbering.

title: Loops and Iteration Tools
q: When does a for loop's else block execute?
options: When the loop finishes without hitting break
Only when the loop body raises
explain: It is the 'not found' branch in search loops.

title: Loops and Iteration Tools
q: What is the complexity problem with `for a in list_a: if a in list_b:` for large lists?
options: It is O(n*m) - use a set for O(n+m)
It is fine because Python is fast
explain: Membership on a list is O(n); with a set it becomes O(1) per lookup.

title: Loops and Iteration Tools
q: `zip(a, b)` with len(a)=5 and len(b)=3 yields:
options: 3 pairs - it stops at the shortest
explain: Zip truncates silently; assert equal lengths when that would be a data error.

title: Loops and Iteration Tools
q: Which is the production-safe retry pattern?
options: while attempts < MAX with backoff and an alert on exhaustion
Recursive retry without a base case
explain: Bounded retries with backoff prevent infinite loops and thundering-herd behaviour.

title: Functions, Arguments and Scope
q: What does `def f(x, bucket=[]):` cause across repeated calls?
options: The same list is reused and accumulates values
A TypeError on the second call
explain: Defaults are evaluated once and stored on the function object.

title: Functions, Arguments and Scope
q: Which call is valid for `def f(a, b=2, *, c=3)`?
explain: c is keyword-only (after *), so it must be passed by name; b can be positional or keyword.

title: Functions, Arguments and Scope
q: What is UnboundLocalError usually a symptom of?
options: Assigning to a name inside a function that was intended to be global
explain: Assignment makes the name local for the whole function scope.

title: Functions, Arguments and Scope
q: Why prefer returning values over printing inside functions?
options: Returned values can be tested, reused and logged; prints cannot
Printing is slower and always wrong
explain: Separation of computation from presentation is fundamental to testability.

title: Functions, Arguments and Scope
q: A closure is:
options: An inner function that captures variables from its enclosing scope
explain: Closures enable decorators, factories and configuration without global state.

title: Lambda, map, filter, Modules and Packages
q: What does `list(map(str, [1, 2]))` return?
explain: map applies str to each element; list() materialises the lazily produced results.

title: Lambda, map, filter, Modules and Packages
q: Why is `f = lambda x: x + 1` discouraged?
options: Named lambdas lose docstrings and readable tracebacks
explain: PEP 8 prefers def for anything that deserves a name.

title: Lambda, map, filter, Modules and Packages
q: What runs when you `import mycars` (a module with a demo print at top level)?
options: The top-level code executes once, including the print
explain: Module top-level code runs once per process on first import; the __main__ block does not.

title: Lambda, map, filter, Modules and Packages
q: Which is lazy?
explain: Generator expressions and map/filter return iterators; the others materialise containers.

title: Lambda, map, filter, Modules and Packages
q: Best reason to move a repeated cleaning step into src/transforms.py?
options: One definition to fix, test and reuse everywhere
explain: Single source of truth is the core argument for modularising data code.

title: Exceptions, Debugging, Files, JSON and pathlib + Foundation Project
q: Why pass encoding='utf-8' explicitly?
options: The platform default varies and can corrupt non-ASCII text
explain: Explicit encoding is the difference between reproducible and machine-dependent parsing.

title: Exceptions, Debugging, Files, JSON and pathlib + Foundation Project
q: Best approach when 1 in 10,000 rows is malformed?
options: Quarantine the row, continue, and report the failure count
explain: Soft failure per row with an auditable report; only schema-level problems should abort.

title: Exceptions, Debugging, Files, JSON and pathlib + Foundation Project
q: `Path('data') / 'raw' / 'x.csv'` produces:
explain: pathlib uses the correct separator per platform and can chain cleanly.

title: Exceptions, Debugging, Files, JSON and pathlib + Foundation Project
q: What is the risk of `except Exception: pass`?
options: Real errors vanish, producing silent wrong results
explain: Silent failure is the most expensive class of production bug.

title: Exceptions, Debugging, Files, JSON and pathlib + Foundation Project
q: Which makes a script idempotent?
options: Overwriting outputs deterministically and creating directories with exist_ok=True
explain: Running twice should produce the same state, not doubled data.
